site.name: Sthapati Ramaswamy Workshop
site.concept: A hereditary atelier of temple architects and stapathis offering vastu-shastra consultation, gopuram restoration drawings, and stone-carving commissions in the Dravida tradition.

card_pattern: Each module is framed by a thin double-rule border in vermilion and gold-leaf, with a small lotus glyph anchoring the upper-left corner and a peacock tailpiece closing the lower-right. Card titles are set in Cinzel small-caps with wide letter-spacing over a sacred-white surface; body copy is Eczar in ink-black. Stepped corner brackets reference the receding tiers of a vimana.
design_rules: Saturated, dense, ceremonial: vermilion and peacock-blue blocks separated by gold-leaf rules, never blank fields. Composition is always tiered and axial — narrowing upward, mirrored left/right, with ornament at every margin. Typography sits like a stone-cut inscription: Cinzel in wide tracking for titles, Eczar warm-serif body, never thin or airy.

pages.title: Sthapati Ramaswamy Workshop — Temple Architects since 1887
pages.content_brief: Hero introduces the workshop as a fifth-generation atelier on East Chitra Veedhi, Madurai, founded by Sthapati Vaidyanatha Ramaswamy in 1887. Three tiered cards summarise the practice: vastu consultation for new mandapas, restoration of gopuram polychromy, and granite figurative carving. Closing band lists current commissions: Rajagopuram repainting at Tiruvannaikaval, a 16-pillared kalyana mandapa near Kumbakonam, and a private Navaratri mandapa for a Chettinad family.

pages.title: The Lineage — Five Generations of Stapathis
pages.content_brief: Genealogical narrative beginning with Sthapati Vaidyanatha Ramaswamy (1854–1919), pupil of the Tanjore court guild, through his son Muthuswami (commissioned for the 1923 Srivilliputhur tier-renewal), grandson Arunachalam (silver medal, Madras Presidency Crafts Exhibition, 1948), down to the current principal Sthapati R. Ganesa-Ramaswamy. Includes a sidebar on the workshop's adherence to the Mayamata and Manasara texts. A photograph caption: 'The drafting hall, East Chitra Veedhi, monsoon 1962.'

pages.title: Practice & Disciplines
pages.content_brief: Detailed catalogue of services: (1) Vastu-purusha-mandala layout for new shrines, with site orientation and proportional schemes drawn in the agama tradition; (2) Vimana and gopuram tier-design from three-talas to nine-talas; (3) Polychrome restoration in saturated vermilion, peacock blue and saffron with gold-leaf finish; (4) Granite and Krishna-shila figurative carving including yali capitals, dvarapalas, and lotus rosettes; (5) Kalasha consecration and finial casting in pancha-loha. Each discipline is described in two paragraphs with typical project duration and the lead craftsman.

pages.title: Selected Works, 1962–Present
pages.content_brief: A chronological project list rendered as inscribed tablets: 1962 — Eastern Gopuram repainting, Sri Anjaneya Temple, Karaikudi; 1978 — New kalyana mandapa, sixteen pillars with yali bases, Srirangam outer prakara; 1991 — Kalasha replacement (nine vessels), Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar private shrine, Theni; 2004 — Polychrome consolidation of seven tiers, Rajagopuram, Srivilliputhur; 2017 — New three-tala vimana for the Chettiar family kuladevata shrine, Athangudi. Each entry has a short note on materials and the principal artisan.

pages.title: The Drafting Hall & Stone Yard
pages.content_brief: Description of the physical premises: a 1903 stone-and-tile structure with an open central courtyard housing the drafting hall (drawings stored in palm-leaf bundles and rolled cartridge paper), the carving yard with eleven granite blocks under cane awnings, and the polychromy room where pigments are still ground from cinnabar, lapis substitute, and turmeric-mordanted lac. Sidebar lists the senior craftsmen by name and specialty: M. Subramaniam (yali capitals, 41 years), Kannan Pillai (polychromy, 28 years), Lakshmi Ammal (kolam-pattern transfer, 19 years).

pages.title: Correspondence & Commissions
pages.content_brief: Address: Sthapati Ramaswamy Workshop, 14 East Chitra Veedhi, Madurai 625 001, Tamil Nadu. Telephone: 0452-234-1887. Workshop hours: Monday to Saturday, 7.00 to 12.00 and 16.00 to 19.30; closed on amavasya and on the principal festival days of Sri Meenakshi temple. Commission enquiries should include site dimensions, intended deity (where applicable), and proposed consecration muhurta. Site visits across the southern peninsula undertaken on retainer; preliminary drawings rendered within forty days of agreement.
